newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission says no decision on French budget.
newsitem.headline: Commission says no decision on French budget.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had not taken a decision on whether France's plan to transfer pension funds to its budget would be acceptable for qualifying its budget for EMU.
"It is not true that the Commission has taken a decision," Patrick Child, spokesman for Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy told Reuters.

Child was responding to questions about a report that an EU financial accounts committee had failed to recommend to the Commission that it accept the French plan to use the money to cut its deficit to GDP ratio in line with EMU qualification criteria.
The mark jumped half a centime in Europe on market talk about the report.
Child said the Commission had received details of what France plans and it was examining them.

An advisory committee of statistical experts from EU member states had met, he said. "In the light of the result of that discussion and the technical considerations...they (EUROSTAT) will take a decision in the next few days or weeks."
Separately, a Commission source said that a number of committees organised by EUROSTAT, the Commission's statistical arm, had been discussing the issue.
The source said the committees had been unable to agree on France's plan, and that a letter had been sent to EU member states asking for their opinion.
"There was no consensus, which is why we have taken a proposal to get the written opinion of member states," the source said.
The source added that the member states had been asked to report back by midday (1100 GMT) on Wednesday so that the information could be given to de Silguy.
De Silguy would announce a decision probably next week, they said.
